pr.title: Fix capture analysis for by-move closure bodies
pr.description:
The check we were doing to figure out if a coroutine was borrowing from its parent coroutine-closure was flat-out wrong -- a misunderstanding of mine of the way that `tcx.closure_captures` represents its captures.

Fixes #123251 (the miri/ui test I added should more than cover that issue)

pr.author: compiler-errors

issues.title: `Unexpected initial operand type` with async closures and `FnOnce`

analysis.summary: The ByMoveBody pass (StateTransform) generates the second, by-move coroutine body used for `FnOnce`/`AsyncFnOnce` calls of coroutine-closures (async closures). Its capture analysis was wrong: it marked inner coroutine captures as by-move based only on `tcx.closure_captures(coroutine_def_id)`, without comparing against the parent coroutine-closure's captures and without accounting for the leading synthetic argument captures. The correction skips `num_args` in the inner capture list, `zip_eq`s the remaining captures with `tcx.closure_captures(parent_def_id)`, and only forces an upvar by-move when the inner capture is by-ref while the parent capture is by-move. It also builds the by-move upvars tuple by concatenating the coroutine-closure arguments with the parent closure's upvars. This fixes #123251, where a by-ref-to-by-ref capture was wrongly rewritten and produced a coroutine type mismatch.
analysis.originalLogic: The pass built the by-move coroutine's `tupled_upvars_ty` directly from every item in `tcx.closure_captures(coroutine_def_id)` via `capture.place.ty()`, and inserted `FieldIdx::from_usize(idx)` into `by_ref_fields` for every capture whose `capture.is_by_ref()` was true, using that capture's index in the full `closure_captures` list. The patch states: "The check we were doing to figure out if a coroutine was borrowing from its parent coroutine-closure was flat-out wrong -- a misunderstanding of mine of the way that `tcx.closure_captures` represents its captures."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation treated any inner coroutine capture that was by-ref as needing to be taken by move from the parent closure, without checking the parent capture mode and without offsetting the field index by the synthetic argument captures. Concretely it used `if capture.is_by_ref() { by_ref_fields.insert(FieldIdx::from_usize(idx)); }` over the whole capture list. The fixed code instead uses `.skip(num_args)` + `.zip_eq(tcx.closure_captures(parent_def_id))` and only inserts when `coroutine_capture.is_by_ref() && !parent_capture.is_by_ref()`, at index `FieldIdx::from_usize(num_args + idx)`. Thus an upvar that is by-ref in both the inner async block and the parent closure must remain borrowed, not be forced by-value. The resulting type error reported in the linked issue begins: "Unexpected initial operand type: expected *mut Coroutine".
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source using the nightly `async_closure` feature (coroutine-closures) where an async closure returns a coroutine body processed by ByMoveBody. Relevant inputs vary along two independent axes: (1) the parent closure capture mode (`move` vs non-`move`), and (2) the inner async block capture mode (by-ref, by-move, or consuming). Include captures of owned values, captures of references (e.g. `let x = &Hello(1); async || { println!("{x:?}"); }`), arguments passed to the async closure, consumed captures that force `AsyncFnOnce`, and closures invoked through both `&impl async Fn()` and `impl async FnOnce()`.
analysis.trigger: Generating a by-move coroutine body for a local coroutine derived from a coroutine-closure whose closure kind is not already `FnOnce`, when the inner coroutine captures an upvar by reference and the parent coroutine-closure also captured that upvar by reference.
preconditions: `body.source.def_id()` is a local coroutine def id and the coroutine type comes from `body.local_decls[ty::CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL].ty`.
The coroutine's kind from `coroutine_args.as_coroutine().kind_ty().to_opt_closure_kind()` is not `ty::ClosureKind::FnOnce` (the pass early-returns for FnOnce).
`tcx.local_parent(coroutine_def_id)` is a `ty::CoroutineClosure`, giving access to `tupled_upvars_ty`, `coroutine_closure_sig().tupled_inputs_ty`, and closure captures.
The inner `tcx.closure_captures(coroutine_def_id)` list includes the synthetic argument captures first, so analysis must `.skip(num_args)`.
The remaining inner captures correspond one-to-one with `tcx.closure_captures(parent_def_id)` and can be checked with `zip_eq` plus a type equality assertion.
pitfalls: Do not infer by-move-ness from the inner capture's `is_by_ref()` alone; compare it with the corresponding parent capture. The patch only forces by-move when `coroutine_capture.is_by_ref() && !parent_capture.is_by_ref()`.

Do not use the raw index from `closure_captures(coroutine_def_id)` as the field index; the inner list is prefixed by the closure arguments. The fixed index is `num_args + idx` after `.skip(num_args)`.

Do not build `tupled_upvars_ty` by mapping every inner capture's `capture.place.ty()`; the by-move coroutine's tuple is the coroutine-closure arguments concatenated with the parent closure's upvars: the patch describes concatenating 'the args + closure's captures (since they're all by move)' and chains the parent upvars tuple after the input tuple fields.
The leading captures are arguments 'by construction', so any zip against parent captures must skip exactly `num_args = tupled_inputs_ty.tuple_fields().len()`.
Skipping body processing when the coroutine kind is already `FnOnce` is expected, because such upvars are already taken by value.
A by-ref capture of a reference is not the same as a by-move/thunk capture; conflating them changes the coroutine's upvars tuple type.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a run-pass UI test (`tests/ui/async-await/async-closures/captures.rs`) with `//@ check-run-results` and a matching `.run.stdout`, plus a mirrored Miri pass test (`src/tools/miri/tests/pass/async-closure-captures.rs`) kept in sync. Drive the coroutines with a deterministic `block_on` and a noop waker. Cover four combinations as the patch does: capture by-ref (owned value and reference), capture and consume to force `AsyncFnOnce`, capture with `move` without consuming, and capture with `move` plus consuming. Call through both `async Fn` (`call(&c)`) and `async FnOnce` (`call_once(c)`). Assert the printed program output; the expected output includes repeated `Hello(0)` through `Hello(5)` lines. This targets the exact type mismatch between the borrowed and by-move coroutine upvars tuples rather than merely checking compilation.
evidence: The check we were doing to figure out if a coroutine was borrowing from its parent coroutine-closure was flat-out wrong -- a misunderstanding of mine of the way that `tcx.closure_captures` represents its captures.
Fixes #123251 (the miri/ui test I added should more than cover that issue)
